sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the northwestern residential blocks of South Amboy, with the grid drawn square to the page and Main, 2nd and 1st streets running across it. North Stevens Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, Potter Street along the left edge and Stockton Street along the right edge, with 4th Street across the top. Blocks numbered 77, 78 and 80 hold rows of frame dwellings with outbuildings on narrow lots, many with a front porch and a rear shed. Public School No. 2 stands at the top left corner, and a Masonic Temple stands in the block east of North Stevens Avenue near the top. South Amboy M.E. Church sits on the corner of 2nd Street, with a gasoline filling station and a row of brick-fronted dwellings on the east side. At the lower left the map turns: Augusta Street runs diagonally across the corner, with a printed compass, a row of dwellings, a manufacturing building labelled Vest Mfg. and St. Mary's Parochial School, whose large brick building is shaded red. The whole of the lower left quarter of the sheet is otherwise blank, belonging to the adjoining sheets 3 and 5. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked along the streets, and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (8, 9, 3, 5) are printed at the margins.
notes: The oblique street at the lower left is Augusta; the grid there is drawn at a different angle from the main grid because the real streets meet at an angle.
Modern names: North Stevens Avenue is Stevens Avenue North; Potter, Main, 1st, 2nd, 4th, Stockton, Church and Augusta are listed under the same names in OpenStreetMap.
The label of Potter Street at the left edge is cut by the sheet edge; the lettering before 'D POTTER' is not readable.
Fitted rotation about 59 degrees, scale 7.8 px per ft.
50 ft, one part, rotation +59: N. Stevens Av, Main, 2nd, 1st, Church, Potter to Stockton.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the central part of South Amboy where the older diagonal street pattern meets the later grid. North Broadway runs down the right-centre of the sheet, bending to run vertically near the bottom; Main, 2nd, 1st and Church streets cross it at an angle, with Stockton Street running across them, and Augusta Street along the foot of the sheet. The blocks between Main Street and Church Street are the commercial and industrial heart of the town: the Sigmund Eisner Co. clothing factory with its cutting room and warehouse, a furniture warehouse, Chas. Komar underwear manufacturing, a dress factory, a motion picture theatre, a hotel, a rug cleaning works, and the lumber and masons supply yard of Miller, Bergen and Welsh Inc. along North Broadway. Institutions include the 1st Baptist Church, the Presbyterian church, a telephone exchange, a bank and a fire department building on the right. The New York and Long Branch railroad runs down the right edge. At the left a heavy-lined box, labelled 2 and 3, contains an area of sheet 2 drawn at a different angle, with St. Mary's R.C. Church and the printed words N. Stevens Av.; the rest of the sheet continues past its lines. Sheet numbers 9, 6, 7 and 2 appear at the margins.
notes: The heavy-lined box at the lower left repeats part of sheet 2 at a different rotation and is cut out of this part's mask.
North Stevens Avenue appears only inside that box.
Main Street / Stockton Street was detected 11 m from its fit and rejected.
Fitted rotation about 31 degrees, scale 7.8 px per ft.
50 ft, one part: Main to Augusta along N. Broadway; heavy-lined box at lower left repeats sheet 2 at another rotation and is masked out; cut at the railroad edge.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the residential blocks on the west side of South Amboy between Feltus and Pine streets, with Augusta Street across the top and George Street along the foot. North and South Feltus Street run down the left of the sheet and North and South Pine Avenue down the right, with David, Henry and John streets crossing between them. Blocks 83, 84, 86, 87, 89, 90, 92 and 93 hold rows of frame dwellings, some with stores. The largest works is C. Poppen and Co., a tobacco and cigar factory with its storage building, shaded red at the centre top beside North Feltus Street. A fire station labelled Protection Hose Co. No. 1 stands at the upper left, and a synagogue stands in the lower left block beside the compass. Main Street appears as an oblique street crossing the upper left corner. Railroad lines and a siding curve across the lower left, below John Street, and a siding runs along the bottom beside George Street. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are marked along the streets. Neighbouring sheet numbers 8, 10 and 11 are printed at the margins, and a compass with a long north arrow is drawn in the left middle.
notes: Pine Avenue here is today's North Pine Avenue; Feltus Street is South Feltus Street (the 'N. Feltus' stretch is Feltus Street North in OpenStreetMap, not used).
Augusta, David, Henry, John and George are printed without a suffix; today they are Augusta Street, David Street, Henry Street, John Street and George Street.
Fitted rotation about 31 degrees, scale 7.7 px per ft; the George Street row is at the sheet edge.
50 ft, one part: Feltus to Pine, Augusta to George.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers four full residential blocks in the centre of South Amboy, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The blocks run between North and South Pine Avenue on the west and North and South Stevens Avenue on the east, and are bounded by Augusta Street at the top of the sheet, then David, Henry and John Streets, with George Street along the bottom; the four blocks carry block numbers 85, 88, 91 and 94. The page is turned so that the long east-west streets run across it, with north towards the upper left. Almost all of the buildings are frame dwellings, mostly one and two storeys, set on narrow lots, with a scattering of stores, small sheds and auto garages behind them; a few brick or tile buildings stand at corners. The one large commercial building is a bus garage with steam heat and electric lights at the corner of North Stevens Avenue and David Street. A junk yard and an auto repair shop sit in the middle of the block between John and George Streets. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches are drawn along the streets with their sizes, and dwelling house numbers are given along every frontage. The streets are each marked 60 or 80 feet wide. Margins show the adjoining sheets: 8 and 2 above Augusta Street, 4 to the west, 6 to the east and 11 below George Street. The scale bar and the copyright line sit in George Street at the foot of the sheet.
notes: South Pine Avenue (south of Henry) is today part of North Pine Avenue; North Stevens Avenue between Augusta and Henry is today Stevens Avenue South.
The street names are printed without suffix (AUGUSTA, DAVID, HENRY, JOHN, GEORGE); today they are Augusta, David, Henry, John and George Street.
50 ft. Central blocks Augusta to George, N./S. Pine Av to N./S. Stevens Av. One part. Pilot sheet (10 of 10 junctions).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the central blocks of South Amboy between North and South Stevens Avenue at the left edge and North and South Broadway at the right edge, from Augusta Street at the top to George Street at the bottom. Blocks 24, 25, 26 and 27 hold mainly frame dwellings in regular rows on narrow lots. The main public buildings are St. Mary's Convent at the upper left, the Post Office and a bank on Broadway, the John St. M.E. Church near the middle, and Public School No. 1 with Borough Hall in the lower left, set in a large open block. The business frontage on Broadway at the right edge includes stores, a post office and a bank, drawn with brick walls and shaded red or yellow. Clinton Pl. runs short below John Street beside the school. A compass is drawn at the top, and the numbers of neighbouring sheets 3, 2 and 7 are printed at the margins. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches follow the streets.
notes: North and South Stevens Avenue are Stevens Avenue North and Stevens Avenue South in OpenStreetMap; Broadway is North Broadway Street and South Broadway Street.
Clinton Pl. is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Augusta, David, Henry, John and George are printed without a suffix.
Fitted rotation about 30 degrees, scale 7.7 px per ft.
50 ft, one part: Stevens to Broadway, Augusta to George.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the east side of South Amboy from North and South Broadway at the left edge to North and South Rosewell Avenue at the right, between Augusta Street at the top and George Street at the bottom. Blocks 12 to 15 hold frame dwellings in rows, with a few stores and workshops. A railroad corridor with several tracks of the New York and Long Branch railroad runs down the left of the sheet beside Broadway, with a siding and a freight yard; Howell and Gordon's coal and wood yard stands beside it. Broadway at the left edge carries brick stores, a freight building and a printing works. A club building stands near the right, and a feed and grain store with a mill is drawn on Henry Street. At the right edge Raritan Bay is shown as a blue shore with the beach, the water running down the right side from Henry Street to George Street. A compass is drawn at the upper right, and the numbers of neighbouring sheets 3, 6, 9 and 12 are printed at the margins.
notes: North and South Rosewell are North Rosewell Avenue and South Rosewell Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Broadway is North Broadway Street and South Broadway Street.
Augusta, David, Henry, John and George are printed without a suffix.
Junctions on George Street were not detected (street at the sheet edge).
Fitted rotation about 30 degrees, scale 7.7 px per ft.
50 ft, one part: Broadway to Rosewell, Augusta to George; Raritan Bay at right.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 8, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, is the main map east of the Pennsylvania Railroad in the north-west of South Amboy. It covers the blocks around North Feltus Street, Walnut, Centre, Cedar and Elm streets at the lower centre, Washington Avenue down the right, and the streets of the upper right, Potter, Thompson, 4th and 5th streets and North Stevens Avenue, whose blocks are drawn at an angle. Blocks 57 to 66, 71, 72 and 76 hold small frame dwellings in rows. The main institutions are the Sacred Heart R.C. Polish Church with its parochial school, a Sisters' Home, a hall and gymnasium and a factory near Washington Avenue. The Bergen Hill passenger station stands at the bottom, where the Raritan River Railroad curves through the sheet below Elm Street, and a cemetery appears at the lower right. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs through the sheet at the left along a heavy line with many tracks, labelled Camden Division. A compass is drawn at the top, with open ground and numbered blocks 58, 59, 60 and 67 shown without buildings. Neighbouring sheet numbers 2, 4, 5, 13 and 69 are printed at the margins.
notes: Centre Street (as printed) was left out of the fit: modern Center Street is displaced from the drawn line (residuals 3 to 6 m).
Main Street and its junctions with Feltus Street and Washington Avenue were not used; they fitted several metres off.
Washington Avenue and Main appear at the right; Main is printed vertically near the right edge.
Fitted rotation about -56 degrees, scale 3.8 px per ft.

100 ft, two parts divided by the Pennsylvania RR: 1 east (Mechanicsville: Stevens, Potter, 4th, 5th, Main, Pine, Feltus); 2 west of the railroad (Raritan, Conover, Alpine, Wilmot, Ridgeway), own north arrow, rotation about -19. Centre St and Main St left out of part 1 (displaced).

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 8, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the scattered housing west of the Pennsylvania Railroad on the northwest edge of South Amboy. The streets are Raritan at the left, Conover in the middle and Railroad Avenue running diagonally beside the tracks, with Alpine Street crossing near the lower middle and Wilmot Street beyond it. Ridgeway Avenue crosses obliquely near the top. Blocks 38 to 45 hold small frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with 4 inch water pipes along the streets. The main line of the Pennsylvania Railroad runs down the right of the part in a wide band of tracks (Camden Division), with a tunnel marked at the top, bounded by a heavy line on the east. A separate north arrow at the upper left shows the part drawn at a different rotation from the main map. The number 13 of the neighbouring sheet is printed at the left edge. Several lots at the lower left and the bottom are blank.
notes: Part 2 is drawn about 35 degrees from part 1, with its own north arrow.
Ridgeway Avenue junctions fitted 5 to 6 m from the others and carry less weight; confidence is medium to low.
The drawn Amboy Secondary railroad lies about 29 m from its modern line.
Fitted rotation about -19 degrees, scale 3.9 px per ft.

100 ft, two parts divided by the Pennsylvania RR: 1 east (Mechanicsville: Stevens, Potter, 4th, 5th, Main, Pine, Feltus); 2 west of the railroad (Raritan, Conover, Alpine, Wilmot, Ridgeway), own north arrow, rotation about -19. Centre St and Main St left out of part 1 (displaced).

sheet-9-1.description: The main map of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the Pennsylvania Railroad yards and the Eastern Coal Dock Co. on the waterfront at the north-east end of South Amboy, where the Raritan River meets Raritan Bay. The page is turned so that north points to the left. Tracks fan out across almost the whole sheet, marked "full of tracks" in two places, and run up to the shore end of the coal pier at the top; a box at the top of the sheet carries the outer end of the pier, about 1000 feet further out. Along the tracks stand the railroad's locomotive house, a machine shop and boiler house with a watchman, a building of the L.E.P. and carpenter shop, a sand dryer, water tanks, and the coal company's two long fire-proof thawing plants, A and B. A freight house and a Y.M.C.A. building stand near the foot of the sheet. A creek or ditch runs down from the shore on the right side. At the right-hand edge a single row of frame dwellings and stores faces Augusta Street, with North Rosewell meeting it; the far side of Augusta belongs to sheets 12 and 7. The lower left corner, around Main Street and Broadway, is left blank for sheets 2 and 3 apart from an inset of this sheet drawn there in a heavy box. Insets for the Bureau of Explosives testing laboratory and the N.J. Central Light and Power Co. plant also sit in boxes on the sheet.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (Augusta Street / North Rosewell Avenue) with the rotation from its measured lines and the nominal 100 ft scale: low confidence away from the right-hand edge.
The Eastern Coal Dock pier and most of these yard tracks no longer exist.

100 ft, north to the left. Pennsylvania RR yards and Eastern Coal Dock Co. on the waterfront. Five parts: 1 main yard (placed from Augusta / N. Rosewell only, anchored); 2 inset top left, Bureau of Explosives testing laboratory on Road to South Amboy; 3 inset top middle, outer end of the coal pier (about 1000 ft out); 4 inset top right, N.J. Central Light & Power Co. super power plant on the Raritan River; 5 boxed inset lower left, Main St / N. Broadway / 2nd St and Christ Episcopal Church, drawn about 28 degrees from the main part.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Bureau of Explosives testing laboratory, Road to South Amboy (no street junction; needs parcel corners or a building surviving today).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: outer end of the Eastern Coal Dock Co. pier (no street junction; pier no longer exists; needs step 6b: offset 1000 ft along the pier from part 1, low value).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: N.J. Central Light & Power Co. super power plant on the Raritan River (no street junction; needs parcel corners of the plant site).

sheet-9-5.description: An inset of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch inside a heavy box in the lower left of the sheet and turned at its own angle, with its own north arrow and sheet number. It covers part of central South Amboy just west of the Pennsylvania Railroad yards: Main Street runs up the left side and North Broadway across the middle, with 2nd Street on the right. The block between Main Street, North Broadway and 2nd Street is drawn in full, with frame dwellings, a few stores and a brick building of three storeys at the North Broadway corner; the New York and Long Branch Railroad and the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks cross its upper end, with a concrete bridge over them. West of Main Street stand Christ Episcopal Church and school and Christ Church Home, both with steam heat and electric lights. Below North Broadway the area is left blank and marked for sheet 3, and the bottom of the inset reaches Stockton Street. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and fire hydrants are drawn along the streets.
notes: North Broadway is today North Broadway Street.

Placed from three detected junctions (Main / North Broadway, 2nd / North Broadway, Main / Stockton): an exact first-order fit with no check point; fitted scale 3.995 px/ft, about 3 percent off the nominal 100 ft.

100 ft, north to the left. Pennsylvania RR yards and Eastern Coal Dock Co. on the waterfront. Five parts: 1 main yard (placed from Augusta / N. Central Light & Power Co. super power plant on the Raritan River; 5 boxed inset lower left, Main St / N. Broadway / 2nd St and Christ Episcopal Church, drawn about 28 degrees from the main part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the western edge of South Amboy where the built-up city thins out into subdivided farmland along the Sayreville Township line. Bordentown Avenue crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right and is the one continuous thoroughfare. South of it, between Division Street and Highland Street, lies a block of mostly frame dwellings with long narrow lots on Prospect and Highland and a ruled-out grid of unbuilt lots near Cross Street at the bottom. To the east, Florence Avenue, Parker Avenue and Ward Avenue run down to Portia Street through blocks of closely built houses, bounded on the right by South Feltus Street. North of Bordentown Avenue the upper left is largely unbuilt: platted lots on Gonologues Lane, Bertram Avenue, Isbell Avenue, Barton Place, Charles, Robert and Campbell Streets show few buildings. In the upper right a gas company terminal (Public Service Gas Co.) sits at George Street, and the South Amboy Memorial Hospital stands north of Bordentown Avenue near Catherine Street. Lefferts and Catherine Streets cross the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees on the page, with a north arrow at left. A dash-dot line marked Sayreville Township runs down the left side. Block numbers 77 to 120 are printed on the blocks.
notes: Gonologues Lane is today's Conlogue Avenue; Cross Street (south edge) corresponds to today's Hillcrest Avenue.
Barton Place is probably today's Catherine Street west of Bertram Avenue (junction matched as Bertram Avenue / Catherine Street, medium confidence).
Printed Portia is Portia Street; printed South Feltus is South Feltus Street today.
Street names were read at overview scale with full-resolution checks on the upper left and centre of the sheet only.
100 ft, one part, rotation +30: Feltus to the township line, George to Division, Sayreville Township.

sheet-11-1.description: Sheet 11, main map, shows the central part of South Amboy between George Street at the top and Portia Street near the bottom. South Pine Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and South Feltus Street along the left edge, with South Stevens Avenue at the right edge. Cross streets from north to south are George, Lefferts, Catherine, Gordon, Ferris, Louisa and Portia Streets. Bordentown Avenue cuts diagonally across the upper half from lower left to upper right. The west half is closely built with frame dwellings, among them a lumber and supply company, a coal yard on the Raritan River Railroad siding, and a fire department building near Bordentown Avenue. The east half is dominated by Raritan River Railroad property: a curved roundhouse, a turntable, a machine shop and a store house, with tracks running to the upper right. South of Louisa Street the blocks east of Pine Avenue are largely vacant with only a few houses, and a cemetery is lettered across the bottom. A water pipe line is drawn in most streets. The scale is 100 feet to an inch and the sheet is turned about 30 degrees on the page. A heavy-outlined box at lower right belongs to another part and is excluded from this mask.
notes: South Pine Avenue on this sheet is North Pine Avenue today north of Portia Street and South Pine Avenue to the south.
Printed South Stevens Avenue is Stevens Avenue South and Stevens Avenue in current data.
Names were read at overview scale; not all checked on full-resolution crops.
100 ft. Part 1 main map (George to Bordentown, Pine to Stevens); part 2 boxed inset at lower right (S. Pine Av, blocks 121/122 at the city limits) unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed inset: South Pine Avenue at the city limits, blocks 121 and 122 (one street, no cross street; needs step 6b: a point carried from sheet-14-1 plus px_per_ft and north_deg).

sheet-12-1.description: Sheet 12, main map, covers the east side of South Amboy along the Raritan Bay shore, between George Street at the top and Portia Street near the bottom. South Stevens Avenue runs down the left edge and South Broadway down the centre. The cross streets are George, Bordentown Avenue (drawn diagonally in the upper half), Catherine, Gordon, Ferris, Louisa and Portia. The upper left is a closely built district of frame dwellings. Gordon and Ferris Streets enclose empty blocks crossed by a curved set of railroad tracks. The Federal Seaboard Terra Cotta Corporation works, drawn in pink and labelled as manufacturers of architectural terra cotta, fills the block between Louisa and Portia Streets with kilns, drying sheds and a row of circular stacks. A wide band of tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad runs north to south through the middle of the sheet. East of the tracks, a row of houses front George Street and the Bordentown Avenue extension, and unbuilt blocks reach the shore of Raritan Bay. A city limits line crosses near the bottom. The scale is 100 feet to an inch and the sheet is turned about 30 degrees on the page. A heavy-outlined box at lower right is a separate part.
notes: Printed South Stevens Avenue is Stevens Avenue South and Stevens Avenue in current data.
Names were read at overview scale; not all checked on full-resolution crops.

100 ft. Part 1 main map (S. Stevens, S. Broadway, Portia to George, Raritan Bay); part 2 boxed inset at lower right: Rosewell with Augusta, David and Henry (the sheet 9 waterfront), placed on three points along Rosewell.

sheet-12-2.description: Sheet 12, part 2, is the boxed inset at the lower right of the page. It shows a small piece of the shore of Raritan Bay with Rosewell Street running up the left side and Augusta, David and Henry Streets crossing it, with a short pier at the end of Henry Street. The blocks are numbered 2 to 4 and are almost empty: one dwelling stands on the Augusta Street block and another south of Henry Street. A heavy box line bounds the inset on the left and top, the tinted water of Raritan Bay lies to the east, and the block numbers continue on sheet 9, where the area is shown in full. The inset has its own north arrow, drawn almost vertical, and is at the same 100 feet to an inch scale as the main map. It repeats, at sheet 12's position, the area printed as part of sheet 9.
notes: Rosewell is North Rosewell Avenue today.
Placed from three points along Rosewell Street (one detected, two hand-picked), so rotation comes from that line only; low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 main map (S. Stevens, S. Broadway, Portia to George, Raritan Bay); part 2 boxed inset at lower right: Rosewell with Augusta, David and Henry (the sheet 9 waterfront), placed on three points along Rosewell.

sheet-13-1.description: Sheet 13, part 1, shows the Melrose district west of Oak Street, at the western edge of South Amboy. The lower left is a regular grid of long east-west avenues, Kearny, Roll, Perrine, Heston and Frazzee, crossed by Clay Street and Oak Street, with houses clustered along the northern blocks and unbuilt lots further south. The Melrose Hose Company building stands at Oak Street and Roll Avenue. The upper left, bounded by a heavy line, holds Laurel and Scott Avenues and Fouratt Avenue, almost all unbuilt, with a lumber shed, auto wreckers and a few dwellings along the State Highway (Road to South Amboy) at the top. Corporation limits are marked along a curved line near the centre. The scale is 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned about 19 degrees from north. The part has its own north arrow.
notes: The State Highway (Road to South Amboy) is US 9 in current data.
The heavy line in the upper left separates blocks that are numbered differently; both sides sit in the same fit.
Frazzee Avenue is Frazee Avenue in current data (not used as control).
Names were read at overview scale.
100 ft, Melrose (Sayreville Twp), rotation about -19. Part 1 west (Clay, Oak, Kearny to Heston); part 2 east (Fouratt, Laurel, Scott, Ridgeway), drawn with a jog along Oak.

sheet-13-2.description: Sheet 13, part 2, is the eastern half of the Melrose sheet. Fouratt Avenue crosses the top; Oak Street, Laurel Avenue and Scott Avenue run south from it toward Ridgeway Avenue, which crosses diagonally from upper left to lower right. Raritan, a street with a regular line of houses, runs down the right edge. The blocks between Laurel and Scott are the most built-up, with frame dwellings, a welding company and a school or hall at the south end; the blocks between Oak Street and Laurel carry narrow lots. A railroad runs diagonally across the left side. South of Ridgeway Avenue the land is largely open. Corporation limits and city limits lines are marked along the right edge. The scale is 100 feet to an inch and the sheet is turned about 19 degrees from north, with the Melrose name lettered at top.
notes: Placed from four detected junctions on Fouratt, Laurel, Scott and Ridgeway; Oak and Raritan junctions with Ridgeway were not detected.
Names were read at overview scale.
100 ft, Melrose (Sayreville Twp), rotation about -19. Part 1 west (Clay, Oak, Kearny to Heston); part 2 east (Fouratt, Laurel, Scott, Ridgeway), drawn with a jog along Oak.

sheet-14-1.description: The upper part of sheet 14, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the north end of the Morgan section of Sayreville Township along Woodland Avenue and Pine Avenue, just south of the South Amboy city limits, which run down the left edge. The page is turned so that north points to the upper left. Cross streets run up the sheet from Pine Avenue across Woodland Avenue: Manor, Grand, Wessco, Nassau Place (marked arbitrary and not opened below Woodland), Grove, Grant, Lincoln and Madison. The blocks are laid out in narrow building lots, numbered 122 to 219, and are only thinly built: a scatter of frame dwellings, a few stores, sheds and garages, and two cement block works, one on Wessco Street and one south of Pine Avenue. At the head of Grand Street, inside a heavy outline, stands the City of South Amboy pumping station, in continuous operation, with steam heat, electric lights and three electric pumps. Woodland Avenue is marked not opened east of Grant. The strip south of Pine Avenue (block 121) is largely empty. The lower half of the sheet, below a heavy line with the compass, continues the map east of Madison Street.
notes: Pine Avenue is today South Pine Avenue; Nassau Place is on the line of today's Bayview Avenue and Grant on that of Jersey Street.
Manor Street was left out of the fit: its modern junctions lie 6 to 8 m off the drawn line (drawn about 205 ft from Grand, today about 258 ft).
The pumping station is drawn in a heavy outline at the head of Grand Street and is placed with this part.

100 ft, north to the upper left. Morgan (Sayreville Twp). Two parts: 1 Woodland Av and Pine Av, Manor to Madison, with the city pumping station at the head of Grand St; 2 (below the heavy line) Madison to Luke and Pine Av curving towards sheet 15, Dolan and Hoffman Avs.

sheet-14-2.description: The lower part of sheet 14, drawn at 100 feet to an inch below a heavy dividing line, continues the Morgan section of Sayreville Township east of Madison Street, at the same angle as the upper part. Woodland Avenue and Pine Avenue run across it and are crossed by Madison, Liberty and Luke Streets; the blocks are cut into narrow lots, numbered 223 to 229, with a few frame dwellings, stores and an auto repair garage. East of Luke Street lies a large empty tract, block 233. Pine Avenue curves up to the right towards sheet 15, and beyond it Dolan Avenue and Hoffman Avenue (marked not opened) leave it with a handful of dwellings and stores in blocks 243 and 297. A building at the foot of the sheet is marked to be removed. The scale bar is drawn at the bottom.
notes: Pine Avenue is today South Pine Avenue.

100 ft, north to the upper left. Morgan (Sayreville Twp). Two parts: 1 Woodland Av and Pine Av, Manor to Madison, with the city pumping station at the head of Grand St; 2 (below the heavy line) Madison to Luke and Pine Av curving towards sheet 15, Dolan and Hoffman Avs.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the Morgan section of Sayreville Township, between South Amboy to the north-west and Chesequake Creek at the bottom. The sheet is turned so that the long blocks of Morgan run down the page. The main street grid occupies the right two thirds: Grove, Willow, Bay (South), Hausling Place, 1st Street, Taft Place, 2nd Street and Applegate Place cross the north-south streets Main, Perrine Avenue, Morgan Avenue and Cliff Avenue, with numbered blocks 136 to 148. Most lots are narrow and empty; houses, a few stores and sheds are scattered along the cross streets, and the Morgan Hose and Chemical Company firehouse stands on Main Street at Taft Place. Two diagonal lines cross the grid: the old Pine Avenue (State Highway) from the upper left and a second State Highway diagonal across the middle blocks, with the railroad beside Main Street at left. In the upper left, Vineyard Avenue and Midland Avenue run up from Pine Avenue past an auto polish works and gas tanks. Main Street (Keyport Road) runs down the left side of the built-up area to a small cluster of houses on Byrom Place and a bridge over a stream that enters Chesequake Creek at the bottom edge. The lower left corner, below a heavy line with the compass, belongs to sheet 16 and is outside this part.
notes: Hausling Place is Haussling Place today; Taft Place is on the line of Feary Place, and Bay (South) is South Street.
The old Pine Avenue diagonal is NJ 35 today; NJ 35 junctions were used in the fit only where they agree with the drawn lines.

Reading made from full-resolution crops of the central blocks, the top left and the bottom centre; the far right edge and the Wampus Street area at the bottom right were read at overview size only and left out.
100 ft, Morgan: Morgan Av and its cross streets, NJ 35; lower-left box (sheet 16 material, Chesequake Creek) masked out.

sheet-16-1.description: The lower part of sheet 16, below the heavy line across the middle of the page, shows the Laurence Harbor section of Sayreville Township at 100 feet to an inch. At the top, the shore of Raritan Bay and Laurence Harbor run across the sheet; the compass lies at the left. Below the shore is a residential subdivision built round Shoreland Circle, a pair of curved streets, with Harbor Way, Twilight Avenue, Ocean Avenue, Sea View Avenue and Beachwood Avenue running between them, and Neptune Place and Laurence Parkway at the left and right ends. Blocks 4 to 10 are filled with narrow lots and a moderate scatter of frame dwellings. A dance hall and bath houses stand on the shore at the right. Below the circle a straight State Highway runs across the whole sheet with a row of lots (block 11) along its north side, and below it the long blocks 250 to 259, mostly vacant, are split by Summerfield Avenue and Rowan Way. Lantana Way runs diagonally to the lower right past Delray Place and Lakeside Avenue. Blocks 251, 252, 254 and 255 are only sparsely built. The scale bar and the Princeton library stamp are at the bottom.
notes: Twilight Avenue, East Beachwood Avenue and Seaview Avenue are the modern names; State Highway is NJ 35, and Rowan Way lies on the line of Shoreline Avenue.
The detected Shoreland Circle junctions fit poorly (residuals of 2 to 7 m) and State Highway (NJ 35) was left out as widened; two Summerfield Avenue junctions were hand-picked.
The part above the heavy line (Morgan Beach, State Highway strip) is a separate part not georeferenced here.
100 ft. Part 1 Laurence Harbor (Shoreland Circle, State Highway, Summerfield Av) below the heavy line; part 2 Morgan Beach strip on the State Highway along Raritan Bay above it, unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Morgan Beach: State Highway strip with bungalows, bridge over Chesequake Creek (no street junction; NJ 35 widened; needs step 6b: parcel corners or carried points from sheet-15).

sheet-17-1.description: Sheet 17 continues Laurence Harbor eastward at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned so that the shore of Raritan Bay runs diagonally across the upper left. Along the shore, Bayview Drive carries a long row of bungalows and cottages built on wooden posts, and a series of parallel avenues leads inland from it: Wilson, Roosevelt, McKinley, Cleveland, Garfield, Lincoln, Monroe, Madison and Jefferson Avenues, ending at Harding Road at the right. Blocks 50 to 61 are laid out in narrow lots and are thinly built except near the shore. Roosevelt Avenue crosses the avenues near the left, with a school or church building drawn in yellow, and Laurence Parkway runs down the lower left past Shadyside Avenue and Ravine Way. Below State Highway, which crosses the sheet in the middle, a second grid of long blocks (12 to 21) is formed by Sunset Avenue, Morningside Avenue, Orchard Avenue, Brookside Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Greenwood Avenue, with Valley Avenue along the bottom edge, where the map continues on sheet 18. Many lots here are empty. At the right, a heavy outline encloses the Oschwald Brick Works, which is a separate inset and is not included in this part.
notes: Ravine Way is Ravine Avenue today; State Highway is NJ 35, not used in the fit.
Harding Road was left out of the fit because its curved junctions were rejected or 7 to 11 m off.
Names read from overview-size lettering plus partial full-resolution crops; spellings of the small avenues were not checked on every crop.
100 ft, Laurence Harbor: Bayview Drive, Valley Av, Laurence Parkway grid; part 2 inset Oschwald Brick Works unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Oschwald Brick Works (no street junction; needs parcel corners of the works site).

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continues Laurence Harbor south of sheet 17. The upper half repeats the long north-south blocks of the grid seen on sheet 17: Valley Avenue crosses the top edge, and Orchard, Brookside, Prospect, Greenwood, Forest and Grove Avenues run down the page to Hilltop Avenue and, below it, to Woodland Avenue. Oakdale Avenue forms the right edge. Blocks 15 to 31 are laid out in narrow lots, mostly vacant, with scattered houses. At the left, Laurence Parkway runs diagonally across the sheet, with Hillcrest Avenue, a second Hilltop Avenue and blocks 38 to 43 beside it. A broad railroad right of way crosses the lower half from the left to the lower right, with the compass at its middle and the scale bar to the right. South of the tracks the streets turn to a different angle: Cook Avenue, Groben Avenue, Palmer Avenue, Lea Avenue, Matawan Avenue, Miller Avenue, Britton Avenue, Arbutus Way and Ely Avenue run between blocks 263 to 286, the right part of them thickly set with small lots and a few houses. A creek runs in from the top right corner.
notes: Oakdale Avenue, Maurer Place and Matawan Avenue, and the unclear names in the lower left corner, are not in today's OpenStreetMap extract and were not used.

Only two junctions south of the railroad (Arbutus Way / Miller Avenue and Cook / Miller, the second undetected) gave control there; the lower district rests on the fit to the upper grid, so its placement is less certain.
Names south of the railroad were read at overview size and the spellings are medium confidence.
100 ft, Laurence Harbor south: Valley, Orchard, Brookside, Prospect, Hilltop, Woodland Avs to Matawan Av and the railroad; one part.
